Test a covariate effect in the gate

Source: R/inference.R
gate_test.Rd

Compares a full gate against a reduced gate in which the effect is removed. With firth = FALSE the statistic is the usual likelihood ratio $$T = 2\{\hat\ell(\hat\gamma_{\mathrm{full}}) - \hat\ell(\hat\gamma_{\mathrm{red}})\}.$$

Usage

gate_test(l1, l0, X, X0 = NULL, firth = FALSE, B = 0L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

l1, l0

Log class likelihoods, one per participant.

X

Full gate design matrix, including an intercept.

X0

Reduced design matrix. Defaults to the intercept alone.

firth

Use the Firth-penalised gate and \(T_{\mathrm{PO}}\).

B

Number of permutations. 0 skips the permutation null. The class likelihoods are held fixed while the covariate rows are shuffled, which is valid because they do not use the covariate.

seed

Optional seed for the permutation draw.

Value

An object of class mbmm_test with the observed statistic, its df, the permutation p_perm and null distribution when B > 0, the chi-squared p_chisq when firth = FALSE, and both fitted gates.

Details

With firth = TRUE it is instead twice the difference of penalised objectives, $$T_{\mathrm{PO}} = 2\{\tilde\ell_X(\hat\gamma_{\mathrm{full}}) - \tilde\ell_{X_0}(\hat\gamma_{\mathrm{red}})\}, \qquad \tilde\ell_X(\gamma) = \ell(\gamma) + \tfrac12 \log |X^\top W(\gamma) X| .$$ Because the two penalty determinants have different dimensions, \(T_{\mathrm{PO}}\) is a penalised-objective difference and not a likelihood ratio. No chi-squared reference is reported for it; use the permutation null, which is valid for any fixed statistic.

See also

fit_gate()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 80; x <- rnorm(n); X <- cbind(1, x)
l1 <- rnorm(n, 0.6 * x); l0 <- rnorm(n)
gate_test(l1, l0, X, B = 99, seed = 1)
#> <mbmm_test>
#>   T (likelihood ratio) = 0.382 on 1 df
#>   chi-squared p = 0.5365
#>   permutation p = 0.51000  (B = 99, smallest attainable 0.01000)
